To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
air temperature is associated with changes in several inflammatory and coagulatory blood markers in men with CHD and PD.

a 10°C decrease of air temperature over 5 days before blood withdrawal led, on average, to a 3% increase in platelet count, a 5% increase in fibrinogen, a 5.5% decrease in C-reactiv protein in patients with pulmonary disease, and a 4.5% decrease of C-reactive protein and a 5% decrease of factor VII in patients with coronary disease.

air temperature is associated with changes in several blood markers, and the complex interplay of these blood markers at low temperatures may contribute to the association between cold and increased cardiovascular risk.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cold air on the human body.
the effects of temperature on blood coagulation and inflammation in two groups of patients.
the effects of air temperature on inflammatory and coagulatory markers and the association with the occurrence of cardiovascular events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a temperature decrease is associated to an increase in inflammatory and coagulatory blood parameters.

a decrease in temperature is associated with a rise of platelet counts and fibrinogen in PD patients, with a decrease in C-Reactive Protein in CHD patients and an increase in factor VII in CHDs without diabetes.

the associations between air temperature and blood markers are complex and that further studies are required to clarify the role of blood markers in temperature-related cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity and mortality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the association of cold with cardiovascular and respiratory diseases is complex.
temperature decrease is linked to changes in several blood parameters and this may contribute to the association between cold and mortality.
the associations between temperature change and blood parameters are complex and may differ between diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cold temperatures are associated with increased levels of inflammatory and co-agulation factors.

the effects of cold on blood parameters differ by disease and may be different in patients with diabetes.
